hints: Look carefully at where each vessel leaves or enters the heart. Which large arch leaves from the centre top (P) and which vessels come from the lungs (Q and R)?

Remember the two exceptions to the rule: the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood and the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood. High oxygen means more oxyhaemoglobin, low oxygen means more haemoglobin.
walkthrough:
**Identify vessels P, Q, R and S**

P is the aorta, the large arch curving up from the left ventricle to the body.

Q is the pulmonary artery going to the lungs, R is a pulmonary vein coming from the lungs, and S is the inferior vena cava bringing blood up from the body.

**Link each vessel to oxygen content**

Oxygenated blood has haemoglobin saturated with oxygen, so it has more oxyhaemoglobin than haemoglobin.

Deoxygenated blood has given up oxygen, so it has more haemoglobin than oxyhaemoglobin.

**Sort the four vessels**

P (aorta) and R (pulmonary vein) both carry oxygenated blood that has just come from the lungs via the left side of the heart.

Q (pulmonary artery) and S (vena cava) both carry deoxygenated blood with low oxygen concentration toward the right side of the heart and then to the lungs.

options.A: P is oxygenated but Q is the pulmonary artery, which carries deoxygenated blood with more haemoglobin than oxyhaemoglobin.
options.B: Both P (aorta) and R (pulmonary vein) carry oxygenated blood saturated with oxygen, so mostly oxyhaemoglobin.
options.C: S is low in oxygen but P is the aorta, which is high in oxygen, so they do not match.
options.D: S is low in oxygen but R is a pulmonary vein, which is high in oxygen, so they do not match.
